name: kernel/genie/genie.ps1
description: Phoenix Genie, the Universal Kernel in PS7 (dot-sourced from the PS7 profile): `genie up/down/restart/status/log/doctor` runs `main_kernel.py` as a hidden background process (FileTree moved to 7713/7714 so it no longer collides with Helix-I on 7703/7704); `genie find`/`clone` pull from the clonepool through packages-worker with the SHA3-512 custody check before any byte is written (no baseline = refused unless `-Force`); `genie import` clones + hot-loads a suit into the running closet; `genie closet` lists it; `genie custody` audits clonepool rows with no SHA3 baseline and writes a reviewed re-intake script. Clone = OUT only — Genie never writes R2/D1.

name: kernel/genie/genie_control.py
description: the kernel's control socket, started by `main_kernel.py:boot()`: 127.0.0.1:8766 only, per-boot token in `~/.phoenix/genie/control.token`, refuses any request with an Origin header. `GET /kernel` (live library/Frank/Helix-I/Helix-E status), `GET /closet`, `POST /suits` (loads a file from `~/.phoenix/genie/closet/` only, after re-hashing it against the SHA3-512 the caller verified; imported suits are read-only unless `write` is asked, never clone/translate/delete/kernel, and can never replace a core suit). Imports persist in `~/.phoenix/genie/imports.json` and are re-verified at every boot — a changed file is refused and reported.

name: kernels/
description: the Linux kernel Helix: `helix_kmod.c` + `dm_helix.c` → `helix.ko` (with `/proc/helix`, dm-helix target), `frank3_slot_a.c`/`frank3_slot_b.c` slot modules, `helix.h` (ioctl ABI), `libhelix/` (`libhelix.c` → `libhelix.so`, `helix.py` ctypes binding), `helix_test.c`, `Makefile`, `README.md`, and scripts `helix_boot.sh`, `install_helix_boot.sh`, `dm_helix_test.sh`, `helix_freedrive.sh`, `helix_phoronix.sh`, `helix_verdict_lean.sh` (Compaq-specific). Built/benchmarked on pbm3/pbm-compaq (see `docs/helix/BENCHMARKS.md`).

name: kernels/helix_boot.sh
description: brings the kernel Helix up and down: loads `helix.ko` + both Frank3 slots, builds the dm-helix device over her origin disk, mounts it. `helix_boot.sh start|stop|status` is the single Helix (device `helix`, settings `/etc/default/helix`); `helix_boot.sh start|stop|status <name>` is a named instance (device `helix-<name>`, settings `/etc/default/helix-<name>`, its own origin partlabel, Strand B image and mount). Since 2026-09-29 several instances share one `helix.ko`; a lock stops two instances racing at boot, and the modules unload only when the last one goes down. `HELIX_WARM_WRITE=1` turns on warm_write for that instance. Never formats anything. Live on pbm-compaq since 2026-09-29 as the road-test pair: helix@ingress (Seagate origin, warm_write on) and helix@egress (Toshiba origin), 3584 MiB Strand A each (plan: docs/plans/compaq-road-test-plan.md).

name: kernels/dm_helix.c
description: the dm-helix device-mapper target (double strand: Strand A in RAM, Strand B on the fastest disk, write-through to the origin). Each device keeps its own state, so named instances run side by side. Optional `warm_write` table keyword (2026-09-29): blocks written through her are read back into Strand A so what came in is warm on first use — used on the ingress instance only. `/proc/helix` and the stats ioctl now publish one combined Dandelion across every live instance (hottest heat, hottest state, deepest compression); per-instance numbers stay in `dmsetup status`.

name: kernels/helix_bigset.sh
description: benchmark: a working set 1.5x the machine's RAM, run once on Helix (`helix_bigset.sh helix [/srv/helix-ingress]`) and once on the plain disk with the normal Linux page cache (`helix_bigset.sh standard <dir>`), fio, caches dropped each pass; results in `~/bigset-<label>-<date>/`. This is the road-test "Helix vs standard caching" test. New on disk 2026-09-30 and not yet committed.

name: package-handler/intake.sh
description: intake/clone/prune CLI (version 1.7.0): hex, sidecar, T1-T4 pool, D1 custody, R2 current + per-version bytes, SHA3-512/BLAKE2b gate. Added 2026-09-29: files over ~95 MB go to R2 in 64 MB pieces through the worker's multipart routes (before that, anything over 100 MB was never uploaded); a version whose bytes are already in R2 is copied inside R2 instead of uploaded again; `intake clone` of a directory works on a machine with no local copy (pulled from R2, checked against D1); a local copy that is out-of-date against D1 is refreshed from R2 on clone (Phoenix stays the authority); directory files are pulled and verified 8 at a time (`INTAKE_PARALLEL`); a re-intaked directory keeps its unchanged files in the snapshot and manifest.

name: package-handler/worker/
description: packages-worker (D1 `phoenix_dev_db` + R2 `phoenix-clonepool`): clonepool, custody, glossary, versions, deps, connections (Atlas), peer review, `/stats`, and as of 2026-10-01 the `/player` node session lifecycle routes. Version 3.6.0 added the `/clonepool/<key>/mpu` multipart routes and `POST /clonepool/<key>/copy`; deployed 2026-10-01 (Version ID `324b61b9-f55f-493a-920f-90978df0aff1`) with the `/player/:uid/*` block. R2 layout for player data: `players/{uid}/state.json`, `players/{uid}/hardware.json`, `players/{uid}/sidecars/{hash}.sidecar.json`, `players/{uid}/blobs/{hash}`. All `/player` routes gated by `PHOENIX_AUTH` bearer token. LOAD: plugs into her Dandelion as its memory-pressure source — max(RAM in use, commit charge) — so her own tiered eviction (raw → zlib 5 → Strand B) follows the machine. EVICTION: watches Strand B fill velocity and spawns Doppelgangers (temporary, self-expiring Strand B budget extensions, sized from eviction speed, capped by free disk minus max(10%, 20 GB)) when B is ≥85% full, predicted full within 120 s, or she refused an allocation; retires them after 10 min once calm and her Strand B data fits without them. Never touches L1/L2/L3, never below her base Strand B. Last 50 decisions kept for `genie status`. Started by `sector1/kernel/main_kernel.py`; `clean_stale_strand_b()` clears Strand B dirs left by force-stopped kernels.

name: radar-worker/
description: `pbm-radar-worker`, Set-Aside Radar: every morning (cron `0 11 * * *`) pulls new SAM.gov set-aside contracts, matches them to each subscriber's work codes, certifications and states, and emails a short digest. Applications are approved by hand (Laurie/Jerry get a one-click review link). Billing: $9.99/month through a Stripe Payment Link + signed webhook; nobody is charged without being asked first (`POST /subscribers/ask-to-pay`). D1 `pbm_radar_db`. Routes and secrets in `radar-worker/README.md`.

name: server.py
description: the server: binds 127.0.0.1 + the mesh address only, Host allow-list (421), CSP `default-src 'self'`, POSTs need `X-Phoenix-Console: 1` + JSON; reads switchboard state with MESH_ADMIN from the vault (never sent to the browser); relays hands calls; serves `/pool/hands.py` to boxes only after checking the bytes' SHA3-512 against D1 custody.

name: hands/hands.py
description: the helper. Windows tools: status, open_app (allow-list), screenshot, restart_pc, cancel_restart. Linux tools: status, services, restart_service (mesh agent / Ollama only), restart_pc, cancel_restart. HTTP `GET /tools`, `GET /log`, `POST /run`; token-gated; `--mesh --allow-from` for boxes; self-update from the hub's clone-pool relay, SHA3-checked and compile-checked, atomic swap.

name: install_remote.py
description: installs hands on a headless box over SSH (bytes over stdin, CRLF stripped), makes the box's token on the box, stores it in `~/.phoenix/hands-tokens.json` on the hub (owner-only).

name: phoenix-hands.service
description: systemd unit on the boxes: `/opt/phoenix-hands/hands.py --mesh --allow-from 10.47.0.2 --update-from http://precision.phx:8470/pool/hands.py`.

name: test_hands.py
description: 7 tests (tiers, fixed per-platform tool list, audit log, self-update refusal paths); runs on Windows and Linux.
